raw_response:
I am 50 years old this year, farming for 30 years on this 12.4 mu plot in Quzhou. I never went to school, can't read or write, but I know my land better than anyone with a diploma. My family has six people — my husband, me, my younger son who still helps on the farm, and my elder son with his wife who work at a factory in Handan. They send home about 2,000 yuan each month, which is how we afford seeds and fertilizer. Without that money, I'd be in real trouble.

I have 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 2.4 mu on the south edge where I grow stevia. The stevia buyer from Shandong has been coming for five years now, pays cash on delivery, so I keep that plot even though it's a lot of hand work.

For wheat, I always plant around October 10th, sometimes a few days later if the maize harvest is delayed. I save my own seed — a red-grained local variety that does well here. I plant about 25 jin per mu, which costs me nothing. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the kind they sell at the cooperative, I don't know the numbers on the bag but it's the red one that most people use. Then in March when the wheat turns green, if it looks a bit yellow I put down half a bag of urea per mu. Last year I skipped the topdress because urea was too expensive, and my yield dropped to about 380 jin per mu. This year my son sent extra money, so I'll do the topdress. I irrigate three times: once after planting if it doesn't rain, once at jointing, and once at heading. Water costs money now with those electric meters on the wells, so I watch the sky, but wheat needs water.

For maize, the window is terrible — sometimes only five or six days between wheat harvest and planting. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, then immediately plant maize with my neighbor's tractor-planter. I pay him 30 yuan per mu for planting. I have to buy hybrid maize seed every year, about 3 jin per mu at 15 yuan per jin. For fertilizer, I can only afford about half to two-thirds bag of compound per mu at planting. I know that's less than what the extension people say, but wheat took most of my fertilizer budget, and maize usually does okay if the summer rains come. If it's very dry at the big trumpet leaf stage, I'll irrigate once. Usually one watering is enough.

For stevia, I transplant new seedlings in late May. The old plants mostly died over winter because I don't have a greenhouse. I buy seedlings from Old Wang in the next village, about 30 yuan per mu worth. It's all hand work — transplanting, weeding, cutting. I put chicken manure and one bag of compound on the whole plot in spring, then a little more after the first cut in July. I irrigate four times, more than the grain crops because stevia needs moisture. I cut twice — mid-July and before frost in October — then dry the leaves on the courtyard. Last year I got about 250 jin dried per mu, and the buyer paid 8.5 yuan per jin. That's good money for such a small plot.

Total spending this year will be around 4,900 yuan. That's almost three months of my son's factory wages. I thought about buying more fertilizer for the maize, but if I get sick or the pump breaks, I need cash in hand. Better to be careful.
